notes: The abstract (data, not checked claims): four decades of Oneida Lake data; multiple regression — age-0 yellow perch winter mortality inversely related to autumn length and to the abundance of alternative prey (gizzard shad and white perch), with no length-selective predation by adult walleye detected; white perch mortality 'directly associated with total predator biomass and abundance of white perch in autumn, and inversely related to yellow perch abundance', not to gizzard shad; winter severity not significant for either; predicted starvation mortality 'much lower than observed' for yellow perch, while similar models for white perch 'were correlated with observed mortality'; conclusion — predation the main mechanism for yellow perch, predation and starvation both possibly important for white perch. The paper's two sentences match this. Not a stand-in: Fitzgerald's 2000 University of Windsor thesis (fetched for Fitzgerald_2000) is on size-selective winter survival of age-0 yellow perch in 18 Great Lakes-basin lake populations (1958–1998); it has no white perch and not this paper's predator/alternative-prey regressions.
